chunks: Then recite the four Talbiyah phrases silently, and they are the obligatory ones. You say: “Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka, wa al-mulka la sharika lak.” These four are obligatory. Then rise and proceed a little. When the land levels out for you, whether you are riding or walking, proclaim the Talbiyah and raise your voice with it. If you have taken the route of al-Madinah and entered ihram from Masjid al-Shajarah, then recite these four obligatory Talbiyah phrases silently until you come to al-Bayda' and reach the milestone on the left of the road. When you reach it, raise your voice with the Talbiyah and do not pass the milestone except while reciting the Talbiyah, and say:

“Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulka la sharika lak. Labbayka dha al-ma'arij, labbayka labbayka tubdi'u wa al-ma'adu ilayk, labbayka labbayka da'iyan ila dar al-salam, labbayka labbayka ghaffar al-dhunub, labbayka labbayka marhuban wa marghuban ilayk, labbayka labbayka anta al-ghaniyyu wa nahnu al-fuqara'u ilayk. Labbayka labbayka dha al-jalali wa al-ikram, labbayka labbayka ilaha al-haqq, labbayka labbayka dha al-na'ma'i wa al-fadli al-hasani al-jamil, labbayka labbayka kashshaf al-kurabi al-'izam, labbayka labbayka 'abduka wa ibnu 'abdayk, labbayka labbayka ya karim. Labbayka labbayka ataqarrabu ilayka bi-Muhammadin wa Ali Muhammad, labbayka labbayka bi-hijjahin wa 'umratin ma'an, labbayka labbayka hadhihi 'umratu mut'atin ila al-hajj, labbayka labbayka ahla al-talbiyah, labbayka labbayka talbiyatan tamamuha wa balaghuha 'alayk, labbayk.” Say this after every obligatory salat or supererogatory prayer, when your camel rises with you, when you ascend a height, descend a valley, meet a rider, awaken from your sleep, mount or dismount, and in the pre-dawn hours. If you omit some of the Talbiyah, it does not harm you, although it is better, except for the obligatory phrases, so do not leave out any of them, and frequently say “Dhi al-Ma'arij.”
When you reach the Haram, perform ghusl from the well of Maymun or from Fakh. If you perform ghusl in your residence in Makkah, there is no harm. And say when entering the Haram:

“O Allah, You have said in Your revealed Book, and Your word is truth: ‘And proclaim the hajj among the people; they shall come to you on foot and upon every lean mount, coming from every deep pass.’”

O Allah, I hope that I may be among those who answered Your call. I have come from a distant journey and from a deep pass, hearing Your call and responding to You, obeying Your command. All of that is by Your grace upon me and Your beneficence toward me, so to You belongs all praise for what You have enabled me to do. By that I seek nearness with You, closeness to You, rank before You, forgiveness for my sins, and repentance from them by Your favor. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, make my body forbidden to the Fire, and grant me safety from Your punishment and retribution by Your mercy [O Most Merciful of the merciful]. Then when you look upon the houses of Makkah, stop the Talbiyah, and its limit is the ascent of the Madinans or near it. Whoever takes the route of al-Madinah stops the Talbiyah when he sees the shelters of Makkah, which is the ascent of Dhi Tuwa. You should engage in takbir, tahlil, tahmid, tasbih, and salat upon the Prophet Muhammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and his family.

key_terms.ذَا ٱلْمَعَارِجِ: A divine epithet invoked repeatedly in the extended Talbiyah.
key_terms.عُمْرَةُ مُتْعَةٍ: The 'umrah performed as part of tamattu' before hajj.
key_terms.مَسْجِدِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ: The miqat from which one entering ihram on the Madinah route begins the specified recitation pattern.
key_terms.ٱلتَّكْبِيرِ: Saying 'Allahu Akbar' in remembrance of Allah.
key_terms.ٱلتَّلْبِيَةُ: The pilgrim's devotional proclamation recited during ihram.
key_terms.ٱلتَّهْلِيلِ: Saying 'La ilaha illa Allah' in remembrance of Allah.
key_terms.ٱلْحَرَمَ: The sacred precinct of Makkah, upon entering which specific acts and supplications are prescribed.
key_terms.ٱلْمَفْرُوضَاتُ: The obligatory phrases that must not be omitted.

ai.seo_question: What are the obligatory phrases of the Talbiyah, when should they be recited, and when does a pilgrim stop saying them?
ai.summary: This passage sets out the rulings and wording of the Talbiyah in hajj and 'umrah, including the four obligatory formulas, when to recite them silently or aloud, and the occasions for repeating them. It also includes a du'a for entering the Haram, instructions on ghusl, and the point at which the Talbiyah is to be discontinued upon approaching Makkah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Then recite the four mandatory phrases of the Talbiyah silently:
"Here I am, O Allah (swt), here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed, all praise, blessings, and sovereignty are Yours. You have no partner."
These four are obligatory. Then proceed for a short while. When you reach level ground, whether riding or walking, proclaim the Talbiyah and raise your voice.
If you are traveling the route of Medina and have assumed Ihram from the Mosque of the Tree (Masjid Al-Shajarah), recite the four obligatory Talbiyah phrases silently until you reach Al-Bayda' and the milestone to the left of the road. When you reach it, raise your voice with the Talbiyah and do not pass the milestone without proclaiming it. Say:

"Here I am, O Allah (swt), here I am. Here I am, You have no partner, here I am. Indeed, all praise, blessings, and sovereignty are Yours. You have no partner.
Here I am, the Possessor of the Highest Ascents. Here I am, the One who initiates creation, and to whom all return. Here I am, the Caller to the Abode of Peace. Here I am, the Forgiver of sins. Here I am, the One to whom we turn in hope and awe. Here I am, You are the Self-Sufficient, and we are the needy before You.
Here I am, O Possessor of Majesty and Honor. Here I am, the True God. Here I am, the One with bounties, excellence, and beauty. Here I am, the Reliever of great calamities. Here I am, Your servant, the son of Your servant. Here I am, O Generous One.
Here I am, seeking closeness to You through Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Here I am, performing Hajj and Umrah together. Here I am, this is an Umrah of Tamattu' leading to Hajj. Here I am, O People of the Talbiyah. Here I am, a Talbiyah that is perfected and accepted by You. Here I am."
You should recite this (the Talbiyah) after every obligatory or recommended prayer, when your mount rises, when you ascend a height, descend into a valley, meet a rider, awaken from sleep, mount or dismount, and during the pre-dawn hours. If you omit some parts of the Talbiyah, it will not harm you, though it is better to recite more of it, except for the obligatory phrases, which must not be omitted. Increase your recitation of "Dhul-Ma'arij" (the Possessor of Ascensions).

When you reach the sacred precincts (Haram), perform ghusl (ritual bathing) at the well of Maymun or at Fakh. If you perform ghusl in your residence in Mecca, there is no harm in that. Upon entering the Haram, say:

"O Allah (swt), You said in Your revealed Book, and Your word is truth: ‘And proclaim the pilgrimage to mankind; they will come to you on foot and on every lean camel, coming from every distant path.’

O Allah (swt), I hope to be among those who responded to Your call. I have come from a distant place and a deep valley, hearing Your call, answering You, and obeying Your command. All this is by Your grace upon me and Your kindness to me. All praise is due to You for enabling me to accomplish this. I seek through it nearness to You, closeness to You, Your pleasure, forgiveness of my sins, and repentance for them by Your grace.
O Allah (swt), bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad. Forbid my body from the Fire, and grant me safety from Your punishment and wrath by Your mercy, O Most Merciful of the merciful."
When you see the houses of Mecca, cease the Talbiyah. Its boundary is at the hill of the Madinites or in its vicinity. If you approach Mecca via the route of Medina, cease the Talbiyah upon seeing the outskirts of Mecca at the hill of Dhu Tuwa.
Engage in takbir (saying "Allahu Akbar"), tahlil (saying "La ilaha illa Allah"), tahmid (saying "Alhamdulillah"), tasbih (saying "SubhanAllah"), and sending blessings upon the Prophet Muhammad and his family.
